records.title: Differences of Signed Representatives: Sharp Answers to Two Questions of Bernert and Arala Santos
records.description:
Let A ⊂ {−n,…,n}∖{0} contain exactly one of k and −k for every 1 ≤ k ≤ n. At the 2025 Oberwolfach workshop on analytic number theory, C. Bernert and N. Arala Santos asked two questions about such sets. First, must A−A contain (1−o(1))n elements of {1,…,n}? Second, for every B ⊆ {1,…,n} with |B| ≥ εn, must the number of pairs (a,b) ∈ A² with a−b ∈ B be ≫_ε n²? We answer both questions affirmatively, with sharp bounds. At most two elements of {1,…,n} are missing from A−A. For every B ⊆ {1,…,n}, the number of pairs (a,b) ∈ A² with a−b ∈ B is at least ⌊(|B|−1)²/4⌋. Both bounds are attained by sets of the form {1,…,a} ∪ {−(a+1),…,−n}, the second for all |B| ≤ ⌊2n/3⌋+1. The proof is a short double-counting argument. This is an unrefereed note.

Unrefereed preprint released for independent mathematical scrutiny. Publication on Zenodo does not constitute peer review. AI-assisted tools supported research, computation, proof development, and manuscript preparation. The author remains responsible for all claims and the final text.

records.title: Even Minkowski uniqueness as a consequence of logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski
records.description: This research note records consequences of OpenAI's recently released origin-symmetric logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality. In every ambient dimension n >= 2 and for 0 <= p < 1, every smooth strictly positive even density on S^(n-1) has exactly one smooth positive even support-function solution of h^(1-p) det(∇²h+hI)=f with positive-definite curvature-radius matrix. For 0 < p < 1, identical Lp surface-area measures determine arbitrary full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies. The note gives the nonsmooth first-variation and mixed-volume strictness argument explicitly and a local form of the smooth endpoint transfer of He–Liu; existence and regularity are established inputs. These results are newly available consequences of the new inequality and known reductions, not a new proof of logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski or a claim of first public announcement. Equal-volume boxes exclude arbitrary-measure uniqueness at p=0. The package contains source, analytic and priority audits, pinned dependency hashes and reproducible exact rational checks. The upstream Lean source scope was inspected, but independent kernel rebuilding, axiom extraction and Comparator reproduction were not completed; no formal verification of this follow-on theorem is claimed. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. This preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing at publication. Automated adversarial reviews are not human peer review.

records.title: Signed impulse estimates and global smooth solutions for finite multispecies relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell
records.description: This research note extends the signed-impulse argument of OpenAI family 362 to a fixed finite number of relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell species with positive masses and arbitrary real charges. It derives the exact source-receiver coefficient, positive mass-weighted energy, angular occupation and selected coefficient bounds, and one coupled momentum bootstrap. The stated global classical theorem assumes nonnegative smooth compact phase data and compatible Maxwell fields with bounded derivatives of all orders and finite energy. The one-species result and its analytic machinery are attributed to OpenAI; mass normalization and continuation are established kinetic theory. No firstness or full Lean-formalization claim is made. AI tools were used extensively in research, drafting and verification. The preprint has not undergone conventional human peer review or refereeing; automated adversarial audits are not human peer review. The universal geometric cancellation is inherited; the new contribution is its species-dependent coefficient transfer and coupled closure for distinct charge-to-mass ratios. Constants may depend on the fixed finite species list; no massless limit or noncompact momentum-tail extension is asserted.

records.title: Finite-energy lattice percolation with internal critical probability one
records.description:
For every integer d at least 2, we construct a nearest-neighbor bond percolation on the integer lattice Z^d whose law is invariant under every graph automorphism and mixing under translations. It has ordinary finite energy: both single-edge conditional states have strictly positive probability given all the other output edges. Almost surely there is a unique infinite component C, but the quenched internal Bernoulli bond and site critical probabilities of X and C equal one. Every independent thinning with retention p below one destroys all infinite components. This gives an affirmative construction for the historical ordinary-energy question of Benjamini, Haggstrom and Schramm, restated in Benjamini's Saint-Flour notes and by Benjamini and Tassion.

The construction develops Haggstrom-Mester's published one-ended-tree summable-flip mechanism. Tree edges are deleted with probability 2^(-s), where s is their finite-side size; a non-tree edge is inserted with probability 2^(-M), where M is the maximum finite-side size along its connecting tree path. This dimension independent rule suppresses every bypass and leaves eventually singleton cut boundaries along each ray. Timar's established equivariant one-ended spanning-tree theorem supplies the all-dimensional input. The note also proves a planar bounded-cutset consequence of the exact fixed-phase midpoint projection of the older Haggstrom-Mester site model, whose unchanged flip rates are 4^(-s). That consequence is a deduction supplied here, not a theorem located in the inspected older paper. No wholly new planar perturbation mechanism, verified first resolution, certified novelty of the all-dimensional rule, or worldwide current-open-status claim is made. No uniform energy bound or failure of every uniform marginal bound is asserted.

The deposit contains a five-page research note and a verification archive with editable source, all 27 frozen original files and three evidence archives with 15 members, six independent analytical or priority audit families, primary-source/version/hash locators, an external-pin inventory verifier and a deterministic rebuild tool. The automated checks reproduce source and archive identities with 11 parser/path rejection controls in normal and optimized modes; they do not certify the infinite mathematical proof or historical priority. Downloaded publications, source extracts, renders, and raw input corpora are excluded. OpenAI tools were used extensively in solving, proof development, drafting, coding, and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint; no completed external human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification is claimed.

records.title: A vertex maximum principle for subcritical reinforcement
records.description:
A self-contained alternative proof of unique strictly positive equilibrium and simultaneous almost-sure coordinatewise homogenization for subcritical graph-based reinforcement. The graph is countable, undirected and simple, with bounded degree; vertex firing rates are positive and bounded above, but their infimum may be zero. The exponent satisfies 0 <= alpha < 1. Initial edge counts are arbitrary finite deterministic positive integers. The proof uses finite-volume vertex minimization, an exact compensated jump transform, and a maximum principle for bounded positive complete vertex trajectories. Unrestricted nonnegative-equilibrium uniqueness is false; the positive statement is an explicitly corrected formulation.

Shuo Qin, arXiv:2610.11780v1, Theorem 1.1 (submitted 8 October 2026), supplies the full positive theorem and broader real initialization. It is prominently credited, together with the matching example in Remark 1.3, the older finite-WARM matching mechanism, and the 2018/2021 partial results of Couzinie and Hirsch. The vertex proof here is different, while the power/incidence and complete-limit strategy are shared structural ideas. Angel-Hermon-Yao work reported by Qin was not available as a verified full manuscript with a public date. Repository PR764 has a server creation date of 5 October 2026, but this does not certify the first public availability of current proof bytes. No first, sole, new-theorem or currently-open claim is made. The final publisher MATRIX chapter body was not obtained; question wording was checked against the official hosted pre-publication version.

The companion archive preserves all 63 frozen candidate files, distinct mathematical and priority reviews, bibliographic receipts, and reproducible integrity and finite diagnostic controls. Computation does not certify the infinite theorem or exhaustive priority. AI tools were used extensively in development, writing, reproduction, verification and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint without external human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification. The note and companion materials are CC BY 4.0.

records.title: Near-one oriented-percolation flow from Bernoulli first-passage estimates
records.description:
For the canonical square-lattice oriented Bernoulli edge-capacity flow, the note derives 1-v(p)~sqrt(2(1-p)) as p increases to one, the asymptotic posed by Aldous and Lenderman in 2004. The sources are the left and bottom boundaries excluding the top-left and bottom-right sink corners; the sinks are the top and right boundaries. Shared vertices are allowed among edge-disjoint paths. The exact finite directed-cut identity, its bounded boundary terms, and the fixed-parameter volume limit followed by the small-defect limit are supplied. The source-stated deterministic L1 flow-density limit is an explicit input; the expectation limit also follows from diagonal superadditivity.

The entire asymptotic is presented as an explicitly attributed corollary of Basdevant-Gouere-Theret's public 2021 strict-site score scaling and weighted-list computation in arXiv:2106.12266v1, Section 3.3, equation (33), with its m=0 numerical terms. A precise model-event inclusion groups outgoing rare-edge marks into independent site marks of probability 2q-q^2. The ordinary undirected first-passage theorem alone is not substituted for the asymmetric cut model with zero-cost backward traversals. This is an application identifying an older-estimate consequence, not a new central rare-defect, Poisson, BK or detour estimate. No novelty, historical-firstness, exhaustive-priority or present-day-openness claim is made. An earlier explicit statement of this particular flow corollary was not located in bounded searches; its first recognition remains unestablished. Exact equation references were checked in the public 2021 v1, not in a retrieved final journal body.

The deposit contains the research note and a verification archive with editable source, all thirty immutable original files and their proof/audit history, the longer BK-Poisson argument, independent mathematical and bounded priority assessments, finite falsification controls, source fingerprints, closed typed inventories, an isolated archival replay launcher and a deterministic ZIP builder. The current launcher distinguishes historical requested flags from measured isolated execution flags. Optional source-only authentication checks all three complete native corpora and four exact primary bodies without executing archival code; those third-party bodies and raw corpora are excluded from the deposit. Finite checks and cryptographic hashes supplement the analytic proof and do not prove the asymptotic or novelty. Compressed-byte reproducibility requires identical inputs and the same Python ZIP implementation and zlib runtime.

The claim concerns the prescribed edge-capacity model, not vertex-disjoint flow, other boundary conventions or other graph families. records.title: A flow reduction for equilibrium uniqueness in rank-one bimatrix games
records.description: For explicitly listed rational bimatrix games of variable positive dimensions and exact rank(A+B)=1, uniqueness of the entire mixed-strategy equilibrium pair is coNP-complete and NONUNIQUENESS is NP-complete, allowing arbitrary degeneracy. A polynomial reduction from nonempty positive-integer PARTITION produces a known strict pure equilibrium and an additional pair exactly in yes instances. The proof applies the Disser–Skutella signed flow counter and the Adsul/coauthors auxiliary zero-sum representation, with a tailored comparison-preserving perturbation, injective simplex encoding and uniform all-minimizer exact penalty. The support package preserves authored original and fresh review evidence. A bounded primary-source audit found no exact match among inspected bodies; worldwide priority remains unknown.

records.title: A designed tree model with a sharp congestion–fragmentation transition
records.description:
We give an analytically tractable designed-tree example motivated by Aldous's conceptual congestion toy-model request. For a bounded-degree binary physical tree with k leaves on each root side and k squared cross-root demand streams, strictly positive linear capacity prices uniquely give the cheapest fixed-topology enlargement carrying doubled unit demands. After design, each stream grows affinely at an independent fixed-law Exp(1) rate. An exact transportation-cut formula and an all-cuts probability estimate confine the joint marginal-admission and spare-connectivity change to an interval of width 16 sqrt(log(k)/k) around mean doubled demand. In the two outer phases every optimizer respectively leaves the whole tree spare or saturates every edge. The window is an upper bound, not an exact critical scaling theorem.

Dense traffic, capacities increasing with graph size, quadratic time variance and normalization by the realized offered-demand slope are essential declared features. No canonical right-model, universal congestion, adaptive-growth, critical-profile or first-transition claim is made. Classical flow/concentration, random transportation, HOT and prior congestion/percolation models are credited, including Aldous's earlier tree-realism reservation. A bounded primary-source priority audit found no authenticated exact earlier construction/theorem in inspected material; the final 1993 Karp-Motwani-Nisan journal body, unindexed/unpublished work and uninspected editions remain limitations.

The paper and source/verification ZIP preserve all 24 original research files, independent flow/probability controls and source comparisons. A new narrowly tested replay derivative preserves the original wrapper, requires exact active second-turn output and permits only explicitly bounded older floating diagnostics and documented metadata/projection differences. Python 3.9.6, NumPy 2.0.2 and SciPy 1.13.1 were tested; unpinned historical bitwise replay is not claimed. The preserved optional priority checker separately requires Python 3.10 or later, was tested with Python 3.14.6 and exactly reproduces its 32 retained controls. The analytic proof does not depend on finite computations.
